title: Complete the dark theme build
prompt:
Fill in the Style Dictionary config that generates Northwind's dark theme. The output must:

- name every variable with the `nw` prefix (`--nw-…`),
- use Style Dictionary's built-in CSS custom properties format,
- contain only the dark semantic tokens, not the primitives loaded through `include`,
- wrap them in the attribute selector that switches any element to dark, written with double quotes inside the single-quoted string,
- keep `var()` references instead of resolved values.
hints: The format name is the same one used in the lesson's build script.
Tokens loaded through `source` are marked differently from tokens loaded through `include`. Which property tells them apart?
The selector is the one from the themes lesson: an attribute selector on its own, without `html`.
explanation: `prefix: 'nw'` adds the namespace to every name. `css/variables` writes custom properties inside the given selector. Filtering on `token.isSource` keeps the dark semantic tokens and drops the primitives, which were only included so references could resolve. `[data-theme="dark"]` lets any element start a dark subtree, and `outputReferences: true` keeps lines like `--nw-color-action-bg: var(--nw-color-blue-400);` so the tier structure survives into the browser.
